findings.problem: 'After the arrest' gets the timing wrong. St. Clair passed the ring and note while constables were in the den, before Boone was seized. Holmes's account says that in those few minutes before the arrest Boone could have communicated with the Lascar.
findings.evidence: [6:212] "I slipped off my ring and confided it to the Lascar at a moment when no constable was watching me"; [6:67] "One mistake had been made in not arresting Boone instantly, as he was allowed some few minutes during which he might have communicated with his friend the Lascar"
findings.fix: BODY: The Lascar who runs the Bar of Gold opium den. For a good rent he let Neville St. Clair use a room there to change into and out of his Hugh Boone disguise, and he was the only person who knew the secret. While the police were in the den, St. Clair secretly gave him the ring and a note for Mrs. St. Clair.

findings.problem: Both cards state 'a letter in his handwriting' as fact. At this gate only Mrs. St. Clair says so. Holmes notes it is 'very unlike his usual writing' and then raises forgery ([6:123]). The claim should be attributed to her.
findings.evidence: [6:118] "It is very unlike his usual writing, and yet I know it well."; [6:123] "Unless this is a clever forgery to put us on the wrong scent."
findings.fix: neville-st-clair BODY: A well-off gentleman of Lee, in Kent, who has been missing since Monday. His wife saw him at a window of the Swandam Lane opium den, and his clothes were found in a room there. Now a note posted at Gravesend, which she is sure is in his hand, has reached her, telling her not to be frightened.  |  mrs-st-clair BODY: Neville St. Clair’s wife, of The Cedars near Lee, in Kent. She saw her husband at a window in Swandam Lane on the day he vanished. She has now received a note posted at Gravesend which she is certain he wrote, and she is sure he is alive.

findings.problem: 'has now been missing from home for two days' comes from Kate's arrival at [6:9]. Paragraph [6:0] is a general portrait, and the card gets ahead of the scene that follows it.
findings.evidence: [6:9] "It’s about Isa. He has not been home for two days."
findings.fix: BODY: Kate Whitney’s husband and one of Watson’s patients. He fell into opium addiction after trying to copy De Quincey’s accounts of opium dreams, and has been a slave to the drug for many years.

findings.problem: The subtitle repeats the name ('Watson’s wife | Watson’s wife') and adds nothing.
findings.evidence: [6:10] "to me as a doctor, to my wife as an old friend and school companion"
findings.fix: SUBTITLE: Kate Whitney’s old school friend

findings.problem: 'Mentioned only.' is an editorial note, not reader-facing prose.
findings.evidence: [6:0] "Isa Whitney, brother of the late Elias Whitney, D.D., Principal of the Theological College of St. George’s"
findings.fix: BODY: Isa Whitney’s late brother, a Doctor of Divinity who was Principal of the Theological College of St. George’s.
